key_insight: The paper argues that AI safety needs new mathematics to make systems legible, steerable, and cooperative with humans, with different math fields contributing to different safety problems.
engineering_relevance: For AI engineers, this frames safety as a cross-disciplinary design challenge: use logic/game theory for cooperation, probability for agency modeling, algebra for learned features, and analysis/geometry for generalization and training dynamics.
method: Organizes AI safety questions by mathematical field
Maps each field to a core safety target: cooperation, world-models, features, and training/generalization
Ends each section with an open problem aimed at mathematicians new to AI safety
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a conceptual survey/invitation rather than experimental data, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: The ideas are high-level and open-problem driven, so translating them into practical safety methods will likely require substantial domain adaptation and empirical validation.
paper_title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians
